title: SIGNS.json — Holy Cringe ru presentation layer
trigger_semantics: user-selected interface language only; never nationality inference

purpose.primary: Render the ru interface as an intentionally absurd, self-deprecating, fourth-wall-breaking Holy Cringe parody while preserving the underlying scientific and archival source records unchanged.
purpose.secondary: Deflate false grandeur in the presentation layer and make the interface visibly unserious without weakening provenance, claim ceilings, negative-result preservation, or source access.

style_engine.name: JANUS_HOLY_CRINGE_RU
traits: bureaucratic nonsense colliding with strict provenance
absurd objects such as stools, kettles, foil hats and nervous CI jobs
style_engine.explicit_non_imitation: No living person's voice, catchphrases, or distinctive style is reproduced or claimed as authorship.
style_engine.source_meaning_rule: The renderer may ridicule its own presentation but must not invert or fabricate the scientific meaning of source records.

fictional_cameo.name: Ванесса Шевченко
fictional_cameo.status: explicitly fictional interface character / composite gag
fictional_cameo.residence: localStorage; occasionally an explicitly fictional village near Sumy
fictional_cameo.function: carries provenance packets, foil and absurd reminders that source authority is not created by presentation

network_binding.meta_registry: ru renderer applies to translated presentation text
network_binding.hrain: same key activates Holy Cringe labels and guidance text
network_binding.inaihr: same key activates Holy Cringe semantic UI and requests remote semantic output in the selected language while preserving sourcePaths
network_binding.ru: clearly marked Holy Cringe parody presentation

non_goals: making false claims about real people
using language choice as evidence of nationality
claim_ceiling: SIGNS defines a satirical presentation mode only. It is not a security boundary, access-control mechanism, nationality detector, scientific result, or evidence of audience behavior.
